result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_estrada_index()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate the Estrada index of the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L24384-L24446){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_estrada_index() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The Estrada index is the sum of exponentials of the eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix: `EE(G) = Σᵢ exp(λᵢ)` where `λᵢ` are the eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix. This index captures the degree of folding or compactness of a network, and is related to subgraph centrality and the number of closed walks. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The Estrada index. Returns 0.0 for empty graphs, 1.0 for single-node graphs. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed (Estrada index is only defined for undirected graphs). ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - time complexity: `O(n³)` for eigendecomposition - the Estrada index is always `≥ n` for any graph with `n` nodes - for graphs with no edges: `EE = n` (all eigenvalues are `0`) - higher Estrada index indicates more closed walks (more "folded" structure) - related to subgraph centrality: `SC(i) = Σⱼ φⱼ(i)² exp(λⱼ)` - EE = trace(exp(A)) where A is the adjacency matrix ## Examples {.doc-examples} A single edge (`K_2`) has eigenvalues `1` and `-1`, so its Estrada index is `exp(1) + exp(-1) ≈ 3.086`: ::: {#af84795d .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph() g.add_node(label="A") g.add_node(label="B") g.add_edge("A", "B") # Returns approximately 3.086 g.get_estrada_index() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3.0861612696304874 ``` ::: ::: A graph with no edges at all has every eigenvalue equal to zero, so its Estrada index always equals the number of nodes: ::: {#19ab97aa .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} isolated = ec.Graph() for i in range(5): isolated.add_node() # Returns 5.0 isolated.get_estrada_index() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 5.0 ``` ::: :::
